body:
Founder real-time: 'how hard would it be to increase the friction some at the edges of blocks by default so its a little easier to stick to platforms? right now the physics are so slippery it can be unreasonably hard to parkour' -> confirmed both a global bump and real per-material friction -> 'do we need to make friction per material? i think we need a separate materials config screen it doesnt really make sense under the levels on the left side bar in the level editor - like how can i change the texture for a material and possibly even update the shader for a material.' S478a: doubled global FRICTION/STOP_SPEED (0.15->0.30, 0.1->0.15) in packages/common/physics.h -- there is no literal edge concept in this physics, ground friction was always one flat constant. S478b: friction is now a real per-material property, not dead per-box data -- new shankpit_materials.friction column (IDUNA migration + Go Material/CreateMaterial/UpdateMaterial + level export MaterialExport), new LevelBoxMaterial.friction (level_boxes.h JSON parser), new g_custom_level_material_friction[] table + friction param on phys_set_custom_level_materials, new PlayerState.ground_friction resolved per-tick in resolve_collision's landing branch from the actual box/material a player is standing on, consumed by apply_friction instead of the flat global constant. Both real call sites (server_apply_custom_level, level_boxes_apply_to_physics) updated. Live-verified with a standalone C test (two synthetic materials, friction 0.02 vs 0.90): resolve_collision resolves ground_friction correctly per box, apply_friction produces a dramatically different velocity-decay curve (0.81 vs 0.00 speed retained after 5 ticks). S478c: new standalone 'SHANKPIT Materials' NOCK tab (ShankpitMaterials.tsx) replacing the old MaterialsPanel nested inside the level editor's sidebar -- full CRUD (edit/delete were already real API calls with no UI wired to them), texture picker sourced from the real texture library, friction field. Level editor keeps only its per-wall material-assignment dropdown. Deployed and live-verified: IDUNA migration applied on restart (GET /api/v1/shankpit-materials returns real friction values, seeded brick/concrete=0.30 wood=0.34 metal=0.14 -- metal deliberately slicker for real gameplay texture), new tab text confirmed present in the rebuilt embedded Go binary. Commits: IDUNA 495cb1e (backend)+0d31d53 (frontend screen)+a767550 (dist rebuild)+0399a79 (changelog); SHANKPIT b6243e7 (physics)+9cab4d3 (changelog). Honest, named gap: the live shankpit-server.service restart needed to deploy S478a/b's native physics changes was NOT performed yet in this pass -- iduna.service WAS restarted (S478c/b backend is live), but the game server restart needs the same explicit founder go-ahead this session already established for shankpit-server (live-workload interruption).

⚓ ☃
title: S478: friction tuning bump + real per-material friction + standalone Materials screen
